profiles.name: Bill Ofenloch
profiles.description: Bill Ofenloch is a New York Catholic peace activist whose work with the Catholic Peace Fellowship and Catholic Worker movement reaches back to the Vietnam War era. He has taken part in nonviolent antiwar and nuclear-disarmament actions, documented Catholic Worker protests, and written about peacemaking in Palestine. Ofenloch was arrested and released after a March 27, 2026 peace witness at the Pentagon.

profiles.name: Clare Schaeffer-Duffy
profiles.description: Clare Schaeffer-Duffy is a Worcester, Massachusetts Catholic Worker, journalist, and peace organizer. She and her family have lived and worked at Saints Francis and Therese Catholic Worker, operated a community bakery and house of hospitality, and organized nonviolent resistance to war and nuclear weapons. She also organizes with the Center for Nonviolent Solutions. Schaeffer-Duffy was arrested and released after a March 27, 2026 peace witness at the Pentagon.

profiles.name: Janette Goering
profiles.description: Janette Goering is the eighteenth person arrested in the Prairieland prosecutions that grew out of the July 4, 2025 noise demonstration at the Prairieland ICE detention center in Alvarado, Texas. Not alleged to have been present that night, she is charged with aiding in the commission of terrorism for giving someone a Faraday signal-blocking bag weeks before the action. Her bond was set at 5,000,000 dollars, reduced to 275,000 dollars after an appellate ruling; she was released in mid-June 2026 after roughly eight months (about 233 to 241 days) in custody. Her state case remains pending.
profiles.finding: Named support campaign photo downloaded, inspected and deployed; matching arrest and case number.
profiles.credit: Support the Prairieland Defendants; photographer uncredited
profiles.rights: Rights unspecified; no open license found; see batch40.json

He told police he was joking and was held in the Bexar County Jail on a 40,000-dollar bond.

profiles.name: Sean Dunn
profiles.description: U.S. Department of Justice paralegal (fired after arrest) who, during the August 2025 federal deployment to Washington, DC under Executive Order 14333, was charged after throwing a Subway sandwich at a CBP agent at a downtown federal protective formation. The DOJ initially sought a felony assault indictment; the DC grand jury declined twice, forcing prosecutors to refile as a misdemeanor. Jury acquitted in November 2025. The "Subway sandwich" trial became a national symbol of the DC federal takeover.
